verse_summaries_en: 2.2: Krishna asked: 'Why are you feeling so weak? You are a brave warrior! These sad thoughts don't help you grow.' | 2.3: Krishna said: 'Don't be a coward! Shake off this small worry and stand up ready to do your duty!'
verse_summaries_te: 2.2: కృష్ణుడు అడిగాడు: 'నువ్వు ఎందుకు ఇంత బలహీనంగా ఉన్నావు? నువ్వు ఒక వీరుడివి! ఈ బాధాకరమైన ఆలోచనలు నీ ఎదుగుదలకు పనికిరావు.' | 2.3: కృష్ణుడు ఇలా అన్నాడు: 'భయపడవద్దు! నీ చిన్న చిన్న బాధలను వదిలేసి, నీ బాధ్యతను నెరవేర్చడానికి ధైర్యంగా నిలబడు!'

verse_summaries_en: 2.1: Sanjaya said: Seeing Arjuna full of compassion, his mind depressed, his eyes full of tears, Krishna spoke these words. | 2.2: Krishna said: My dear Arjuna, how have these impurities come upon you? They are not at all befitting a brave man.
verse_summaries_te: 2.1: సంజయుడు ఇలా అన్నాడు: కరుణతో నిండి, కన్నీళ్లు పెట్టుకుంటూ విచారిస్తున్న అర్జునుడిని చూసి, కృష్ణుడు ఈ మాటలు పలికాడు. | 2.2: శ్రీకృష్ణుడు ఇలా అన్నాడు: అర్జునా, ఈ క్లిష్ట సమయంలో నీకు ఈ బలహీనత ఎక్కడి నుండి వచ్చింది? ఇది వీరులకు తగినది కాదు.

verse_summaries_en: 2.4: Arjuna said: How can I fight against Bhishma and Drona, who are worthy of my worship? | 2.5: It would be better to live in this world by begging than to enjoy life by killing such noble teachers.
verse_summaries_te: 2.4: అర్జునుడు ఇలా అన్నాడు: ఓ కృష్ణా, నేను పూజించదగిన భీష్ముడిని మరియు ద్రోణుడిని యుద్ధంలో బాణాలతో ఎలా ఎదిరించగలను? | 2.5: గొప్పవారైన గురువులను చంపడం కంటే, ఈ లోకంలో భిక్షాటన చేస్తూ బ్రతకడం మేలు. వారిని చంపి పొందే భోగాలు రక్తంతో తడిసినవే అవుతాయి.

verse_summaries_en: 2.7: I am confused about my duty. Tell me for certain what is best. I am Your disciple. Please instruct me. | 2.8: Even if I were to win unchallenged sovereignty of a prosperous earth or even lordship over the Devas, I do not feel that it would dispel the grief that withers up my senses.
verse_summaries_te: 2.7: కర్తవ్యం పట్ల నాకు సందేహం కలుగుతోంది. ఏది శ్రేయస్కరమో నాకు ఖచ్చితంగా చెప్పు. నేను నీ శిష్యుడిని, నన్ను శాసించు. | 2.8: Even if I were to win unchallenged sovereignty of a prosperous earth or even lordship over the Devas, I do not feel that it would dispel the grief that withers up my senses.

verse_summaries_en: 2.11: Wise people do not worry about the living or the dead. | 2.12: There never was a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor any of these kings. Nor will there be any time in the future when all of us shall cease to exist. | 2.13: As the soul passes from boyhood to youth to old age, it passes into another body at death.
verse_summaries_te: 2.11: శ్రీభగవానుడు ఇలా అన్నాడు: అర్జునా, నువ్వు విచారించకూడని వాటి కోసం విచారిస్తున్నావు. జ్ఞానులు జీవించి ఉన్నవారి గురించి కానీ, మరణించిన వారి గురించి కానీ దుఃఖించరు. | 2.12: There never was a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor any of these kings. verse_summaries_en: 2.14: The contact of the senses with their objects, O Arjuna, gives rise to feelings of cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go, never lasting long. Endure them, O Arjuna. | 2.15: For, he whom these do not affect, O chief of men, and to whom pain and pleasure are equal - that steadfast man alone is worthy of immortality.

Endure them, O Arjuna. | 2.15: For, he whom these do not affect, O chief of men, and to whom pain and pleasure are equal - that steadfast man alone is worthy of immortality.

verse_summaries_en: 2.16: The unreal never comes into being, the real never ceases to be. The truth about these two is seen by the seers. | 2.17: Know that to be indestructible by which all this is pervaded. No one can cause the destruction of this immutable.

verse_summaries_en: 2.18: These bodies of the Jiva (the embodied self) are said to have an end, while the Jiva itself is eternal, indestructible, and incomprehensible. verse_summaries_en: 7.1: The Lord said, "With your mind focused on Me, taking Me as your support, and practicing yoga—how can you, without doubt, know Me fully? verse_summaries_en: 7.17: Of these, the man of knowledge, who is ever with Me in Yoga and devoted to the One only, is the foremost; for I am very dear to the man of knowledge, and he is also dear to Me. | 7.18: All these are indeed generous, but I deem the man of knowledge to be My very self; for he, integrated, is devoted solely to Me as the highest end. | 7.19: At the end of many births, the man of knowledge finds refuge in Me, realizing that 'Vasudeva is all.' verse_summaries_en: 8.1: Arjuna said, O Supreme Person, what is Brahman? What exists in the individual plane? What is action? What is said to exist in the physical plane? And what is said to exist in the divine plane? | 8.2: O Madhusudana, how is the entity existing in the sacrifice here in this body, and who is it? And how are You to be known by people of concentrated minds at the time of death? | 8.3: The Blessed Lord said, "The Immutable is the supreme Brahman; selfhood is said to be the entity present in the individual plane. By action is meant the offerings that bring about the origin of existence of things."

verse_summaries_en: 8.8: O son of Prtha, by meditating with a mind engaged in the yoga of practice and not straying away to anything else, one reaches the supreme Person existing in the effulgent region. | 8.9: He who meditates on the Omniscient, the Ancient, the Ruler, subtler than the subtle, the Ordainer of everything, of inconceivable form, effulgent like the sun, and beyond darkness—he attains the Supreme Person. | 8.10: At the time of death, having fully fixed the Prana (vital force) between the eyebrows with an unwavering mind, and being imbued with devotion as well as the strength of concentration, he reaches that resplendent Supreme Person.

verse_summaries_en: 9.4: This entire universe is pervaded by Me, in an unmanifest form. All beings abide in Me, but I do not abide in them. | 9.5: Yet, beings do not remain in Me. Behold My divine Yoga. I am the sustainer of all beings, yet I am not in them. It is My will alone that causes their existence. | 9.6: As the powerful element air, moving everywhere, ever remains in the ether, know that so too all beings abide in Me.

verse_summaries_en: 9.13: But the great-souled ones, O Arjuna, who are associated with My divine nature, worship Me with an unwavering mind, knowing Me to be the immutable source of all beings. | 9.14: Aspiring for eternal communion with Me, they worship Me, always singing My praises, striving with steadfast resolution and bowing down to Me in devotion.

verse_summaries_en: 9.17: I am the father, mother, creator, and grandfather of the universe; I am the purifier. I am the syllable Om, as well as Rk, Saman, and Yajus. | 9.18: I am the goal, the supporter, the Lord, the witness, the abode, the refuge, and the friend. I am the origin, the dissolution, the basis for preservation, and the imperishable seed.

verse_summaries_en: 9.22: Those who, excluding all else, think of Me and worship Me, aspiring after eternal union with Me, I look after their prosperity and welfare (Yoga and Ksema). | 9.23: Even those who are devoted to other divinities with faith in their hearts, worship Me alone, O Arjuna, though not in accordance with the Sastras. | 9.24: For, I am the only enjoyer and the only Lord of all sacrifices. They do not recognize Me in My true nature; hence, they fall.

verse_summaries_en: 9.26: If one offers Me with love and devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, I will accept it. | 9.27: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give away, whatever austerity you practice, O Arjuna, do that as an offering to Me. | 9.28: Thus equipped in mind with the Yoga of renunciation, you will free yourself from the bonds of Karma, productive of both auspicious and inauspicious fruits. Thus liberated, you will come to Me.

verse_summaries_en: 9.30: If even the most sinful man worships Me with undivided devotion, he should be regarded as holy, for he has rightly resolved. | 9.31: Quickly, he becomes righteous and obtains everlasting peace. Affirm on My behalf, O Arjuna, that My devotee never perishes.

verse_summaries_en: 11.24: When I behold You touching the Supreme Heaven, shining, multicolored, with yawning mouths and large, resplendent eyes, my inner being trembles in fear. I am unable to find support or peace, O Vishnu. | 11.25: Viewing Your mouths, presenting awe-generating fangs and looking like the consuming fire of final destruction, I know not the quarters of the globe nor do I find repose. Be gracious, O Lord of the Devas! O Abode of the universe!

verse_summaries_en: 11.30: Devouring all the worlds on every side with your flaming mouths, you lick them up. Even without you, none of the warriors arrayed in the hostile ranks will survive."

verse_summaries_en: 14.5: The Gunas of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas arise from Prakrti and bind the immutable Self in the body, O Arjuna. | 14.6: Of these, sattva, being without impurity, is luminous and free from morbidity. It binds, O Arjuna, through attachment to pleasure and knowledge. | 14.7: Know, O Arjuna, that Rajas is of the nature of passion springing from thirst and attachment. It binds the embodied self with attachment to action.

verse_summaries_en: 14.8: Know that Tamas is born of false knowledge and deludes all embodied beings. It binds, O Arjuna, with negligence, indolence, and sleep. | 14.9: Sattva generates attachment to pleasure, Rajas to action, O Arjuna. But Tamas, obscuring knowledge, generates attachment to negligence. | 14.10: Prevailing over Rajas and Tamas, Sattva predominates, O Arjuna. Prevailing over Tamas and Sattva, Rajas predominates. Prevailing over Rajas and Sattva, Tamas predominates.

verse_summaries_en: 14.14: If the embodied self dissolves when Sattva prevails, then it proceeds to the pure worlds of those who know the highest. | 14.15: (a) When Rajas is prevalent, one meets with dissolution and is born among those attached to work. idea: Life is like a growing tree
verse_summaries_en: 15.1: Krishna says: Imagine a magical tree upside down! Its roots are in the sky and branches grow downward. Understanding this tree means understanding life. | 15.2: The tree spreads everywhere, and its roots tie people with their actions—like habits that keep growing.

Is it Sattva, Rajas, or Tamas?" | 17.2: The Lord said, "The faith of embodied beings is threefold, born of their own nature and constituted of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. Each person consists of faith; whatever their faith is, that is who they are.
